content.user_title: Navigate DBX Studio AI Tool Integrations
content.value_statement: DBX Studio teams need a reliable map of AI tool definitions, providers, and execution paths. This skill points Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to the relevant implementation areas.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the DBX Studio file that stores AI tool definitions.
Identifies the DBX Studio file that handles tool execution.
Lists the documented AI tools and their required parameters.
Maps AI providers to the files and functions that handle tools.
Summarizes format conversions for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Bedrock tools.
Outlines the documented steps for adding a new AI tool.
limitations: It is a reference document, not an automated code generator.
It covers only the files and flows named in SKILL.md.
It does not validate database permissions or provider credentials.
It does not execute tests or inspect runtime behavior.

use_cases.title: Trace Tool Definitions
use_cases.description: Find where DBX Studio defines AI tools before making a backend change.

use_cases.title: Align Provider Support
use_cases.description: Compare provider tool formats before updating OpenAI, Anthropic, or Bedrock integration logic.

use_cases.title: Review Tool Additions
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed tool change touches definitions, execution, and provider conversion paths.

prompt_templates.title: Locate Tool Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-tools reference to show where DBX Studio stores AI tool definitions and execution logic.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Current Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-tools reference to list the available DBX Studio AI tools and explain each required input in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Plan New Tool Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-tools reference to create a checklist for adding a new DBX Studio AI tool across definitions, execution, and provider formats.

prompt_templates.title: Review Provider Tool Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-tools reference to compare how DBX Studio sends tool definitions to Anthropic, OpenAI, and Bedrock.

output_examples.input: Where do I add a new AI tool?
output_examples.output: The skill points to the definition file, the executor switch, the handler function, and the provider conversion paths.
The skill highlights Anthropic, OpenAI, and Bedrock format conversions, plus the provider files named for the tool flow.

output_examples.input: What DBX Studio tools are documented?
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes schema reading, table preview, SELECT query execution, chart generation, table description, and table statistics.

best_practices: Start with the referenced definition and executor files before changing provider adapters.
Check every provider conversion path after adding or renaming a tool.
Keep tool descriptions and required parameters consistent across provider formats.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a tool is available for every provider without checking conversion paths.
Do not update only the tool list when execution logic also needs a handler.
Do not treat this reference as a substitute for tests and permission review.

faq.question: Does this skill run DBX Studio tools?
faq.answer: No. It is a reference skill that points to documented files and workflows.

faq.question: Which tools does it document?
faq.answer: It documents schema reading, table preview, SELECT query execution, chart generation, table description, and table statistics tools.

faq.question: Which providers are covered?
faq.answer: It names AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Qwen, Ollama, Gemini, Groq, and DBX Agent.

faq.question: Can it help add a new tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides the documented sequence for updating definitions, execution logic, handlers, and provider conversions.

faq.question: Does it include security controls?
faq.answer: No. It does not describe authorization checks, input validation, or credential handling.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
